title: Pick up and roll a die
instruction: Pick up the small coloured die and roll it on the table. Release it so a marked face turns from facing up to facing down while free, then leave it untouched until it stops.
context: Picking up and rolling a die is a component of assisting someone with tabletop games. This task tests the physical manipulation; it does not require a particular face value or test statistical randomness or fairness.
setup: Two YAM arms in the calibrated station scene; oak-coloured horizontal tabletop 1.10 m by 1.30 m, surface z=0.7475 m, centred at x=0.36 m and y=0 m. One homogeneous 16 x 16 x 16 mm, 5 g cube represents a plastic die. Its collision-free visual face markings are +Z: white/1 pip, -Z: yellow/6 pips, +X: red/2, -X: cyan/5, +Y: green/3, -Y: purple/4. Its centre starts at (0.20, 0.16, 0.7555) m with identity orientation. World x points away from the arm bases, y left, z up. Object jitter is zero. A separate review-only 1600 x 1280 camera is at (0.84, -0.25, 1.55) m looking toward (0.25, 0.17, 0.90) m; the three policy cameras retain their original settings. Render-only tabletop and vertical ruler guides have 5 mm ticks, 10 mm major ticks and a 30 mm height reference, with no collision or support geometry. Perspective must be accounted for when using the guides. No other loose objects or rolling aids are present.
scoring: Version roll-a-die-v3. Each TCP is between the gripper pads, 13 mm short of their tips along the approach axis; distances are to the die centre. 0.25: hold the die with its bottom at least 30 mm above the tabletop for 0.20 continuous seconds with at least one measured TCP less than 35 mm away and normalized opening below 0.30. 0.5: after pickup, release it with its bottom at least 10 mm above the table and both gripper TCPs at least 50 mm from its centre. 1.0: after release, one identified face points upward within 30 degrees, then the same face points downward within 30 degrees (its known opposite face pointing upward is equivalent visible evidence); subsequently the die rests on a face for 1 continuous second. Rest permits at most 2 mm position change and 5 degrees full orientation change from a fixed rest-window anchor, with face tilt at most 10 degrees, bottom within 3 mm of tabletop and both TCPs at least 60 mm away. Post-release TCP re-entry inside 50 mm or leaving the permitted tabletop area invalidates all credit. Held rotation, flat spin and repeated small rocking do not satisfy turnover. JUDGING.md explains the video/ruler protocol; scoring.py defines exact predicates.
run_limit: 1,200 control steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz), one episode per run.
reset_notes: Restore the cube to its specified pose and both arms to the station ready pose. run.py creates a fresh temporal scorer after every reset. Use a new log directory for each run.
fidelity: Homogeneous sharp-edged cube approximates a plastic die; pips are visual only. Rounded corners, dimples and calibrated contact/friction are absent. Fixed-layout demo does not establish random/fair outcomes. Scoring samples at 20 Hz and may miss faster motion. TCP clearance is a contact proxy; full video must also rule out contact with other robot links. Review-only close-up and scale guides aid judging.
scores: Scorer v3, seed 0, identical scene/action limits. Dream-1 run 002: 0.0, 1,200 actions/60.00 s; no qualifying pickup (184.133 s wall). Scripted demo 002: 1.0, 182 actions/9.10 s (44.457 s wall). Both measured trajectories replay to these scores; full audit in VALIDATION.json.
